A PlotNua Guide · Part of Living in the Garden
Garden Room Prices in Ireland
What garden rooms are advertised for, what those prices cover, and how to compare two quotes.
From PlotNua’s research snapshot of · Page updated
The Short Answer
How much does a garden room cost in Ireland?
So treat it as a guide to what is advertised, then use the checklist further down to
turn any price into one you can actually compare.
Published Prices
Garden room and garden office prices by what the price covers
The same building can be sold three different ways: as a kit you assemble, delivered and
built for you, or finished turnkey.
Each is a different purchase, so prices are grouped
by what the supplier says the price includes, and never mixed.
Garden offices sit in
the same groups: a garden office is a garden room bought for work, and is priced the same way.
One Number
Why It Is Hard
Why advertised garden room prices are hard to compare
Before you can tell whether one garden room is dearer than another, you have to know
what each price covers.
Most of the time, that is not published.
Price per square metre does not solve it.
Rooms priced on different bases, or with a
different finish inside, can be several times apart per square metre, so a figure like
that says more about what was left out than about value.
Outside The Price
What can sit outside the advertised price
These are the costs that most often separate an advertised price from a final
quotation.
Whether each one applies depends on the supplier and on your garden.
VAT
Many published prices do not say whether VAT is included.
On a building
of this kind that can be a large part of the bill, so confirm it in writing.
Foundations and groundwork
A garden room needs a level, load-bearing base.
Some suppliers build it, some price it separately, and some leave it to you.
Sloping
or soft ground, access for machinery and removing soil can all add to the work.
Delivery
Some prices include delivery nationwide, some only within a region,
and some charge by distance.
Tight side access can also mean extra handling.
Installation
A kit price leaves the building to you or to a builder you hire.
A “supplied and erected” price may still stop short of the interior finish.
Electrical connection
A room can come wired inside but not connected to your
house.
The cable run from your consumer unit, and the certificate for that work, are
often quoted separately.
Building Regulations and planning
Above 25 m² a garden building must
meet the Building Regulations in full, and the planning exemption has its own size and
position limits.
Both can change the specification you pay for.
Living in the Garden explains the rules
Before You Commit
A garden room quote checklist
Ask every supplier the same questions, in writing, before you compare their prices.
Is VAT included in this price?
Is the base or foundation included?
If not, what does it need, and who builds it?
Is delivery to my address included, and is my side access suitable?
Is the building put up by your own team, or is this a kit?
What is finished inside: insulation, lining, flooring, sockets, lighting, heating?
Is the electrical connection to the house included, with its certificate?
What is the floor area, measured inside and outside?
Does this design stay within the planning exemption for my garden, and does it need to
meet the Building Regulations?
What warranty applies, and to which parts?
Is this a “from” price?
If so, what does the version I want cost?
If two suppliers give different answers to the first four questions, their prices were
never comparable in the first place.
A Different Question
Garden homes are a separate price question
A garden home, a detached building someone can live in, has a different set of rules
since July 2026: its own size range, conditions and notices, and the Building
Regulations in full.
Very few are advertised with a price yet, so this guide does not
put a figure on one.
Living in the Garden
explains what
changed in 2026 and how the garden room and garden home rules differ.

The Research
How these figures were made
This is not a census of the Irish garden room market.
It describes what PlotNua’s
research holds, and a supplier that publishes no price cannot appear in it.
Suppliers are
not named or ranked here, and PlotNua has no commercial arrangement with any of them.
